title: The Concept of Social Structure and Institutions
text:
Social structure refers to the stable patterns of relationships and institutions that influence behavior within a society. It provides the framework, or scaffolding, upon which individual actions are organized, determining roles, status hierarchies, and predictable interactions. These structures include kinship systems, educational networks, and economic marketplaces.

Institutions are formal systems of norms and practices that fulfill basic societal needs, such as law (legal institutions) or marriage (familial institutions). They operate through shared agreements and cultural expectations rather than enforced physical constraint alone. The stability and rigidity of these structures are key concepts in understanding social inertia; change requires significant disruption to established patterns.

Furthermore, power dynamics are inextricably linked to social structure. Those who maintain control over defining resources—be they economic capital, knowledge, or legal authority—are able to define the parameters of acceptable behavior for all members of the collective.
